practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: Despite class-level Javadoc claiming Given-When-Then, the test method body contains no Given/When/Then comments or BDD-style naming and covers only a minimal scenario. Decision rule 3 (tests are minimal/basic) marks it non-compliant for lacking evidence of deliberate prioritized design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only interacts with public API methods of Grafo and does not use reflection or check private/internal state. There is no sign of coupling to implementation internals, satisfying the criteria for maintainable, behavior-focused tests.

Assertions lack descriptive failure messages and rely on default messages (assertNull/assertEquals without message). Decision rule 1 (assertions with messages <50%) applies and the test is marked non-compliant for insufficiently descriptive assertions.

There is no commented-out code and the class has concise class-level Javadoc. The test method is small and does not contain excessive or misleading comments, satisfying the criteria for minimal useful commenting.
The test does not use randomness, current time, sleeps, or external dependencies. It uses local deterministic operations on Grafo and therefore appears deterministic per decision rules.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local variables and does not persist data or modify static/global state. There is no file or DB interaction visible; thus it has no observable side effects and is compliant per decision rules.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class uses @Category(UnitTest.class) annotation at the class level, providing meaningful categorization and fulfilling the practice requirements.
